info.title: Pizza 4P's POS Till API
info.description: The `/api` surface the till, the kitchen display and POS Station call on a store's edge, generated from the handlers (ADR-0177). A device presents its pairing token as a bearer token, and most routes also need a person signed in on it. A refusal is plain text, with its AIP-193 reason in the `pos-error-reason` header where the edge names one.

post.summary:
`POST /api/bills/{id}/fees/{fee_id}/waive` — waive one of an open bill's fees, citing a reason
(ADR-0159 decision 5).
post.description:
Answers with the bill as it now stands, in the shape of its check, so the till redraws it from
the edge's arithmetic and never subtracts the fee itself: the fee's tax goes with it. A fee
that is not waivable answers `409 FEE_NOT_WAIVABLE`, one the bill does not charge
`409 FEE_NOT_ON_BILL`, and a bill that is not open `409 TRANSITION_REFUSED`.

requestBody.description: `reason_code_id`, with `approver_code` and `approver_pin` of somebody who may waive the fee where the person acting may not. Both are secrets and are never logged

post.summary:
`POST /api/bills/{id}/merge` — fold other bills into this one, which survives
([ADR-0128](../../../../docs/adr/0128-a-bill-splits-and-merges.md) decision 5).
post.description:
The path names the **target**: it is the bill the cashier is standing in front of, and it keeps
its identity. Every absorbed bill must be open and on the same table, which is a floor
restriction rather than a model one — settling moves a table, and a bill over two tables makes
"which table moved?" a question with two answers — and of the same order, which two counter
bills, sharing no table, need too: a settle charges a bill's lines from its own order, so
another order's would be charged nothing. Each is refused `409` before anything is written.

requestBody.description: `absorbed_bill_ids`: at least one open bill, on the same table and order, to fold into this one

different act, with its own event, its own reason code and its own permission once the kitchen

post.summary: Mints the code for the next device, replacing whatever code was live.
post.description:
# Why this route exists

A code is minted once per process start and nothing else minted another, so adding a second till
to a trading store meant restarting the service — which drops every till's and kitchen display's
`/ws` session and forces the outbox to drain
([ADR-0117](../../../../docs/adr/0117-a-headless-store-keeps-a-log.md) §70). This removes all but
the first of those restarts: the first device on a virgin box still uses the boot code, because
it has nothing to authenticate with, and every device after it is minted for from inside the
store.

# What it deliberately does not do

It writes **no file** and logs **no code**. `POS_EDGE_PAIRING_FILE` is the headless *boot* path
and this caller is neither headless nor booting — it is a manager holding a tablet that just
received the reply. Minting does unlink that file, because the code it named is now dead
([`Pairing::mint`]).

The log line carries no employee id either. A durable log records identifiers and counts, and a
per-employee managerial-activity stream on a shop-floor box is the thing ADR-0117 §6 kept off
disk; who admitted a device is answered by the durable pairing record, not by this line
([ADR-0118](../../../../docs/adr/0118-one-credential-per-box-and-the-cloud-learns.md) §5).

# What it records for later

The [`Minter`] rides on the code, and the redemption splits it: the **device** this request came
from is named on the cloud-bound `device.admission.granted` event, and the **employee** signed in
on it is written to the store's own `paired_devices` row and goes no further. Both facts are
known only here, at mint time — the tablet that redeems presents six digits and nothing else.

tablet a row is — the device's name lives in the cloud's approved-device registry, and a store
that has never synced has none — so the console shows when each paired and marks the caller's own
row, which together are enough to recognise the odd one out.

The token digest is never returned: it correlates a device across restarts and buys the console

AgentResponse.description: What the claim did, in the vocabulary the till renders.

BatchCloseRequest.description:
Closing several counted drawers at once: their shifts, one approver for those that are other
tills' (ADR-0167 decision 10), and a reason for each drawer whose over or short the store asks
one of (decision 12).

BatchCloseResponse.description:
What a batch close answers: each drawer closed, and what came of the one slip for all of them
where the store combines its close report.

allOf.description:
The same figures and fee lines the table and order reads answer with, so a till draws all
three the same way.

order_line_ids.description:
The order lines it covers ([ADR-0128](../../../../docs/adr/0128-a-bill-splits-and-merges.md)
decision 1), so a till can show a guest what their part of a split table is for.

state.description:
`BILL_STATE_OPEN` while it still owes. A settled, voided, split or merged bill owes nothing
more, and the figures are then what its lines came to rather than a sum to collect.

BillCheckResponse.description: What one bill owes, where it has got to, and which lines it covers.

BillFeeLine.description:
One fee as a settled bill records it
([ADR-0159](../../../docs/adr/0159-a-fee-is-configuration.md) decision 4): which fee, under
which code and name, what it charged, and the tax on it.

The name is the rule's own as the bill froze it, so a copy of the receipt prints what the
original did after the fee is renamed, as a line's name does (ADR-0129, ADR-0144). No event
carries a translation.

code.description: The rule's code, what a report groups fees by.

display_name.description: The rule's own name, as the bill froze it.

fee_id.description: The fee rule that charged it.

tax.description:
The tax on it: its part of the tax of every class it is taxed at. Zero for a fee that is
not taxed.

tax_components.description:
That tax by component
([ADR-0168](../../../docs/adr/0168-a-settled-bill-records-its-tax-components.md) decision 3):
the tax on each of its class shares split as that class's tax line is, then summed by name
and rate, so they sum to `tax`.

Left out when empty, and absent is not zero: it reads as *not split*, which is every fee
charged before this field existed and every fee taxed at rates with no components. A
reader that meets a name it cannot read takes the fee as not split too, and still reads the
bill.

BillId.description: A `BillId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

BillResponse.description: A bill as returned to a device after a command.

drawer_open.description:
What came of opening the cash drawer on a settle that took cash: `OPENED`, `NO_DRAWER` or
`DRAWER_UNAVAILABLE` ([ADR-0165](../../../../docs/adr/0165-cash-paid-in-and-out-is-counted-in-the-drawer-and-a-no-sale-opening-needs-a-manager.md)). Absent when no cash was taken, because nothing
was asked of the drawer.

receipt_number.description: The gapless receipt number, once settled. Never a legal invoice number.

receipt_print.description:
What came of that print: `PRINTED`, `NO_PRINTER`, `PRINTER_UNAVAILABLE`, `UNPRINTABLE_TEXT`,
or absent when the settle asked for no receipt (ADR-0100). Until this field existed the till
rendered "Printing receipt…" over a store with no printer wired at all.

table_state.description:
The state the bill's table moved to, absent for a counter order that has no table
(ADR-0093). The UI already treated this as optional.

BillTaxComponent.description:
One named part of a settled tax line's tax, or of a fee's
([ADR-0168](../../../docs/adr/0168-a-settled-bill-records-its-tax-components.md) decision 3):
`CGST` at 9 % and the tax it accounts for.

name.description: The component, as the `tax` node names it.

rate_basis_points.description: Its part of the rate, in basis points.

BumpRequest.description: A bump as a KDS asks for it: the order, the station, and the lines it made.

BumpResponse.description: What a bump returns: the order, station, and the lines now marked prepared.

BusinessDate.description: A business date, YYYY-MM-DD, by the store's own cutoff

column.description:
The button's zero-based column on a fixed grid, absent for a flowing layout where order alone
places it.

label.description: The caption to show, which may be shorter than the item's catalog name.

menu_item_id.description:
The item this button orders — the id the price book from `GET /api/menu` carries. Layout
names the item; the price book prices it; the two meet only here.

row.description: The button's zero-based row, absent for the same reason as `column`.

BuyerRequest.description:
The buyer a till captured for a corporate invoice.

Personal data, every field of it, so it goes to the store's subject store and never into an
event — `Deserialize` only, with no `Debug`, because a derived one would put a buyer's name into
the axum rejection message for a malformed body.

CategoryResponse.description: One display category: a tab or section on the till.

buttons.description: Buttons placed directly under the category — a flat category has only these.

name.description: The name to show on the tab.

waivable.description:
Whether the fee's rule, as the bill froze it, lets staff waive it on one bill
([ADR-0159](../../../../docs/adr/0159-a-fee-is-configuration.md) decision 5). The till offers
**Waive** only on an open bill's waivable fee, and the edge refuses any other.

CheckFeeLine.description: One fee as the till shows it: the line the settle records, and whether staff may waive it.

CheckResponse.description: What a table owes, as the till shows it.

discount_total.description:
What has been taken off, once a bill is open to take it off. Two figures rather than one,
because the receipt prints them on two lines and for two different reasons — a discount is
a price decision, a comp is food given away. Zero until something is applied, which is every
bill until somebody reduces one.

fee_lines.description:
Each fee charged ([ADR-0159](../../../../docs/adr/0159-a-fee-is-configuration.md) decision 4),
in rule order: the rule, its code and its name, what it charged and the tax on it, as the
settle records them, except that the name is the store's display language where the
current rule translates it. Part by part for a table whose bill is split, as each part
computes its own. Empty where no fee applies, which is every bill at a store with no
`fees` node. The till shows each line, and its total is still `total_due`. A fee waived on
the bill charges nothing and is not listed (decision 5).

subtotal.description: The sum of the order's live line totals, before tax.

tax_total.description: The tax on those lines, each class rounded once by the domain.

total_due.description: What the guest owes — the figure the bill will settle against.

oneOf.description: Asking the cloud for a claim.

cloud.description: The cloud this box will belong to.

oneOf.description: Showing a code for a person to bind at the console.

cloud.description: The cloud whose console binds it.

expires_at_ms.description: When it stops working, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

oneOf.description: The cloud could not be reached; asking again shortly.
Claimed: the box is this store now, and the store server starts next.

store_id.description: The store it was claimed for.

ClaimStatus.description: What the claim page shows, as `GET /api/claim` answers it.

CloseRequest.description:
A close's optional body: the approver for another till's drawer, and the reason for an over or
short the store asks one of (ADR-0167 decision 12).

CodePage.description:
The character set a printer's firmware can render directly.

Anything outside it becomes a bitmap. The list is short because it only needs to cover
what the fleet actually contains; an unrecognised page is
[`CodePage::Unsupported`], which forces bitmap rendering for everything and is therefore
always safe.

CountRequest.description: The blind count: the physical cash counted, in minor units. Nothing about what was expected.

CounterLineResponse.description: One line of an order, for a cashier to recognise what they are charging for.

bill_id.description:
A bill already open on this order. The screen settles **this** bill rather than opening a
second one, which the domain refuses.

queue_number.description:
The daily number staff shouted. Absent for an order that was never given one, which is why
the route reads the number rather than allocating it.

CourseId.description: A `CourseId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

CourseResponse.description: One course, as the till offers it.

course_id.description: The course's identifier, which an item above names and a fire-by-course sends.

display_name.description:
The name to show, already in the store's display language — the same resolution the item's
and the group's names get ([ADR-0074](../../../../docs/adr/0074-localization-and-tax.md)).

sort.description:
Where it falls in the service sequence, ascending.

Carried as well as pre-sorted, because a screen that filters the list still needs to know the
gaps, and rebuilding the order from position in a filtered list is how one screen disagrees
with another about what comes first.

CurrencyCode.description: An ISO 4217 currency code: three upper-case letters

DeviceId.description: A `DeviceId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

DiscountRequest.description:
A discount as a till asks for it: how much, why, and the manager standing at the till for it.

The approval is optional in the shape and required by the act today, exactly as a line void's
is. No store publishes a discount ceiling, so the domain reads the ceiling as zero and every
discount needs `billing.discount.override_ceiling` — but the till sends the same request either
way, and the edge answers `403` when the manager is the missing piece. When a ceiling is
published, a discount under it will start succeeding without one, with no change here.

amount.description:
How much comes off, in minor units. Never a percentage: `billing.discount.applied` records
an `amount`, so a percentage would have to be resolved somewhere, and resolving it at the
till would put the arithmetic on the device that does not own the price book (§14.2).

DiscountResponse.description:
What the bill comes to once the discount is on it — the edge's own arithmetic, so the till never
subtracts a discount from a total itself and arrives at a different tax.

fee_lines.description:
Each fee on the bill once the discount is on it, as the check reads list them: a
percentage taken after discounts moves with the discount (ADR-0159).

DisplayCategoryId.description: A `DisplayCategoryId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

DisplayName.description:
A human-readable name for a product, category, modifier or campaign.

Tenant content, resolved per language in the configuration tree. Admissible in an
event payload because a line snapshot must capture the name shown to the guest at
the moment the line was added — changing or deleting a menu item afterwards must
not alter an open order or a settled bill.

DisplaySubcategoryId.description: A `DisplaySubcategoryId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

DrawerOutcomeSchema.description:
What came of opening the cash drawer (ADR-0165). `NO_DRAWER` is a store with no drawer marked,
the ordinary case; `DRAWER_UNAVAILABLE` is a drawer that should have opened and did not.

DrawerResponse.description: One drawer: absent `terminal_device_id` and `name` for the store's one drawer.

opened_clock.description:
The shop's wall clock when its shift opened, `HH:MM` in the store's timezone, for the till to
show as it is: a till's own clock may keep another zone. Absent while the drawer is closed.

oneOf.description: Its shift, `null` while the drawer is closed.

drawer_access.description:
`DRAWER_ACCESS_ASSIGNED` where each drawer is one person's for its session (ADR-0167
decision 9), so the till asks whom another till's drawer is for and tells a person's own
drawer by `assigned_employee_id`. Absent where drawers are shared, as before.

drawer_model.description: The model the edge runs: `DRAWER_MODEL_PER_STORE` or `DRAWER_MODEL_PER_TERMINAL`.

terminal_device_id.description:
The till this device is, whose drawer is its own, where the store keeps a drawer per till.
Absent for a device that is no till, and where the store keeps one drawer.

waiting_drawer_model.description: The model the store has published, while open shifts keep the edge on the other.

EmployeeId.description: A `EmployeeId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

EventId.description: A `EventId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

FeeCode.description:
A short, stable, language-independent handle for a fee, such as `"SERVICE"` or `"PACKAGING"`.

What a report groups fees by and a CSV export prints, so an operator reads a handle they chose
rather than a ULID. Unlike [`crate::reason_codes::ReasonCode`], which no event carries, it is
admissible in an event payload ([`crate::pii`]): ADR-0159 has a bill record the code of every
fee it was charged, in its frozen rules (decision 3) and its settled fee lines (decision 4). It
names a charge, as a [`DisplayName`] names a product, and never a person.

FeeId.description: A `FeeId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

FireRequest.description:
Which station a fire goes to. Optional: the edge derives the station from the published routing
(ADR-0072), and this is only the fallback for a store with no station plan yet — an absent field
lets the plan decide entirely.

FloorArea.description: A named region of the floor — a terrace, the main hall — with the tables it contains, in order.

tables.description: The tables in this area, in display order.

FloorPlan.description:
The store's floor plan: its areas and the tables in each.

An empty plan is a store whose floor has not been published yet — the edge keeps whatever it holds
rather than blanking the room (the never-blank config contract, ADR-0072).

FloorResponse.description: The store's floor and kitchen plans, as the in-store UI reads them.

seated_times.description:
When the guests at each seated table sat down, keyed by table id, for the tables somebody is
sitting at — how a floor plan says "seated 25 min", which a host reads to know who is due a
check and who is about to leave.

Here rather than on the live orders, because it is a fact about the table and a table is
seated before anything is ordered: the live read lists orders with lines, so a till that
reloaded over a table sat down a minute ago would have had no time for it. Read from the
table's order id ([`Edge::seated_since`]), so every device shows the same figure however long
it has been running.

stations.description:
The kitchen stations and item→station routing, each station with the threshold its board
marks a ticket late after ([`resolved_thresholds`]).

table_states.description:
What each table is doing right now, keyed by table id: free, occupied, awaiting payment,
needs cleaning.

Beside the plan rather than inside it, because the two are different kinds of fact. The plan
is *configuration* — what the console published, the same for every device, changing when
somebody edits the floor. A table's state is *live*, changes every time a guest sits down,
and belongs to this store's projection. Folding it into `FloorPlan` would have put a running
value into `pos-proto`'s published shape and made a device's reload rewrite config.

Sent because a device that has just started has **no other way to learn it**. The states
reach a running till on the fan-out, and a till that was not running when the guests sat down
never saw those events — so before this, a reload drew every occupied table as free, on the
home screen, and a server could seat a table that already had people at it.

FloorTable.description:
One table on a floor plan: its identity, the label a host reads, how many it seats, and where it
sits in the visual editor's grid.

label.description:
The label a host and guest read: "T1", "Bar 3". Presentation text, carried here so the UI
never re-reads anything to draw the floor.

position.description:
Where the table sits in the floor editor's grid. `None` for a table not yet placed — it exists
and can be seated, it just has no pinned position. Omitted from the wire when absent, the same
optional-field shape [`crate::display::DisplayButton`] uses.

seats.description:
How many covers the table seats. Zero means unspecified — a table still seats guests, the
capacity is just not recorded.

table_id.description: The table's identity — the id a `sales.order.opened` event carries and a QR token binds.

GridPosition.description: Where a button sits on a POS terminal's fixed grid: zero-based `column` and `row`.

Health.description: The health payload. Every field is either compile-time constant or a store identifier — no PII.

protocol_version.description: The cloud–edge wire protocol this binary speaks.

status.description: Always `"ok"` when the process can answer at all.

IntegrationResponse.description: One connection, as the Devices screen lists it.

family.description: The family's wire token; `INTEGRATION_FAMILY_UNSPECIFIED` for one this build does not know.

KitchenStation.description: One kitchen station a fired line can route to.

backup_station_id.description:
The station a ticket falls to when this station's printer is down — the backup-printer failover
target a dispatcher consults. `None` means no failover: a ticket for this station stays here.
A backup must name a *different* station in the same plan (enforced by `pos_core::floor`).

late_after_seconds.description:
How long a ticket at this station waits, in seconds, before the kitchen display marks it
late. Read it through [`KitchenStation::late_after_seconds`], which reads an absent value, or
one outside [`LATE_AFTER_SECONDS`], as [`DEFAULT_LATE_AFTER_SECONDS`]. Left off the wire
while absent, so a station that sets none is written as before.

station_id.description:
The station's identity — the `station_id` a `sales.order_line.fired` event carries and a
kitchen `PrintJob` is addressed by (`pos-ports`, ADR-0026).

ticket_language.description:
The language this station's kitchen tickets print in: their fixed labels, and each item's and
modifier's name where the menu translates it. The same choices as a receipt's. Read it through
[`KitchenStation::ticket_language`], which reads an absent or unknown value as the store's
display language. Left off the wire while absent, so a station that sets none is written as
before.

LayoutResponse.description: The store's presentation plan for this channel, as the in-store UI reads it.

categories.description:
The display categories, in the order the console arranged them. Empty when nothing has been
laid out, which the till reads as "draw the flat price book".

LeasedJob.description: One leased job, as the agent receives it.

address.description:
Where to open it: a host and port for a network printer, a device path for a directly
attached one ([ADR-0103](../../../../docs/adr/0103-directly-attached-printers.md)).

capabilities.description: What the **edge** assumed this printer can do when it prepared the document below.

claim_expires_at.description:
Unix milliseconds after which this lease lapses and the job returns to the queue. The agent
has until then to write the bytes and acknowledge.

connection.description: Which of those it is. The agent picks its transport from this and nothing else.

job.description:
The finished document. Its `job_id` is what the acknowledgement carries — deliberately not
repeated at this level, because two copies of an id are two things that can disagree.

printer_device_id.description:
The printer to open. Not on the job — a [`PrintJob`] names a *station*, and a receipt has
none at all.

LeasedJobs.description: What a claim returned. Always present, possibly empty: an empty park is the ordinary answer.

LineRequest.description: A line as a device asks for it to be added — the amounts captured from the menu it holds.

modifier_menu_item_ids.description:
The modifiers chosen for this line. Optional, so a device that sends none — or an older one
that does not know the field — adds a bare line exactly as before. What it changes is the
kitchen: a fired line consumes the base recipe **plus** one recipe per modifier (§8), so a
line that omits them is a line whose extras are never taken off the shelf.

note.description: The guest's note for the kitchen: at most 200 characters, one line (ADR-0157).

note_present.description: Deprecated by `note`: a device that sends only the flag still records that a note exists.

LineResponse.description: A line as returned to a device after a command.

station_id.description: The station the published routing sent this fire to, absent on an add (ADR-0072).

ticket_print.description:
What came of the kitchen ticket: `PRINTED`, `NO_PRINTER`, `PRINTER_UNAVAILABLE` or
`UNPRINTABLE_TEXT`. Absent on an add, which prints nothing (ADR-0100).

LiveLineResponse.description: One line of an open order, with everything a screen needs to draw it and act on it.

bumped.description:
Whether a station has marked it prepared. Orthogonal to `state`: a fired line is still fired
once it is made, and this is what stops a kitchen display re-showing a ticket it has bumped.

course_id.description:
The course the line goes out on, absent for a line on none (ADR-0130). Omitted when absent,
for the reason `seat` is.

Without it a till that reloaded mid-service drew every line uncoursed, so the course controls
offered to send starters the screen no longer knew were starters — the same loss `seat` was
added here to stop, one field over.

fired_time.description:
When the line went to the kitchen. Absent while it is still on the pad, and omitted from the
wire when absent, the way every other optional field on this route is.

The one number a kitchen board is for: which of eight tickets has been waiting longest. Taken
from the firing event's envelope rather than from any clock a screen owns, so a board that
reloads mid-service still counts from when the food was actually ordered — and two boards
side by side agree.

line_total.description: The extended total captured when the line was added — the figure the guest was quoted.

modifier_menu_item_ids.description:
The modifiers chosen for the line (ADR-0127), as ids — the caller names them from the price
book it already holds. Always present, empty for a line that carries none, so a reader never
has to tell "no modifiers" apart from "an older edge that did not say".

note.description: The guest's note while the edge holds it. Omitted when absent, for the reason `seat` is.

note_present.description:
Whether a guest note was written for the line. Always present, because `true` with no `note`
is a note the edge lost to a restart, which a screen must say rather than hide (ADR-0157).

order_line_id.description: The id a fire, a void or a bump is addressed to.

seat.description:
The seat the line was ordered for, absent for the table's. Omitted from the wire when absent,
the way every other optional field on this route is: a `seat` of zero is not "no seat", and a
null would be a second spelling of the same nothing.

station_id.description:
The station the line was fired to, absent while it is still on the pad. Omitted when absent,
for the reason `seat` is. What a kitchen board filters on, so a bar screen that reloads shows
the bar's tickets and not the grill's.

bill_id.description:
A bill already open on it, so a device that reloads on the payment screen settles **that**
bill rather than asking for a second one the domain would refuse.

open_bill_ids.description:
Every bill still open on it, oldest first: one for an ordinary table, one per unpaid part
once its bill has been split (ADR-0128). `bill_id` names only the newest, so a device that
reloads mid-split finds the other parts here. Always present, empty when nothing is open.

sales_channel.description:
The channel it was opened on, a `SALES_CHANNEL_*` token: the counter shows a walk-in the book
of its channel, and whether the guest eats in or takes away (ADR-0160 decision 2). Absent for
an order the edge cannot name a channel for.

table_id.description: The table it sits on. Absent for a counter order, which has none.

LocaleResponse.description: The store's money settings, as the in-store UI reads them.

cash_denominations.description: The notes a guest hands over, ascending, in minor units. Empty means the exact amount only.

cash_rounding_increment.description:
What the grand total is rounded to in cash, in minor units, or `null` for no rounding.

The till does not apply this — `pos_core::billing` does, and the rounding is already inside
the total the check reports. It is here so the screen can *show* the adjustment as its own
line, which is what makes a rounded bill reconcile for the guest reading it.

currency_code.description: The currency every figure on this till is denominated in.

currency_exponent.description:
How many decimal places that currency has: `0` for the đồng and the yen, `2` for the paisa
and the cent ([ADR-0134](../../../../docs/adr/0134-a-currency-says-how-many-decimals-it-has.md)).

Sent because a till cannot work it out. Every figure it draws and every figure a cashier
types is an integer in the minor unit, and without this the screen has to guess where the
decimal point goes — which it did, from a three-row table that had no row for the rupee.

display_language.description:
The store's display language (a BCP 47 tag from the `locale` node), absent when it has set
none. A till that has never been told otherwise starts in it, so a Vietnamese shop does not
open every reload in English.

number_format.description:
How this store writes a number
([ADR-0136](../../../../docs/adr/0136-a-store-publishes-how-it-writes-numbers.md)): the decimal
mark, the group mark, and how many digits go in a group.

Sent for the reason `currency_exponent` is — a till cannot work it out, and the one it
invented was `en-US` for every store in every country. Nothing on the screen reads it yet;
the till follows in its own change, because it alters a figure a cashier is looking at.

prices_include_tax.description:
Whether the prices on this store's menu already contain their tax
([ADR-0104](../../../../docs/adr/0104-multi-component-and-inclusive-tax.md)).

MenuItemId.description: A `MenuItemId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

MenuItemResponse.description: One sellable item, priced and taxed as this store sells it.

available.description:
Whether the item can be sold right now. An item present but 86'd is shown and refused, not
hidden, so staff can see why it cannot be ordered.

course_id.description:
The course this item goes out on, or absent for an item on none (ADR-0130).

An id, not a name: the courses are listed once on the response below, for the reason the
modifier groups are. The till reads it to group an order into starters, mains and desserts,
and to know which lines a fire-by-course will send.

display_name.description: The name to show the guest, already in the store's display language.

menu_item_id.description: The item's identifier, which a line names.

modifier_group_ids.description:
The modifier groups the till must ask about before this item is sold
([ADR-0127](../../../../docs/adr/0127-modifier-groups-reach-the-edge.md)).

Ids, not copies: the groups themselves are listed once on the response below, because one
"Size" group attached to forty pizzas would otherwise be forty copies of the same rule on
every menu read.

sold_out.description:
Whether staff marked it sold out at this store, which `available` already accounts for.
Carried apart so a till can offer to restore it: an item the console published as
unavailable is not the till's to bring back.

tax_class_id.description: The tax class, carried onto the line.

oneOf.description:
The rate for that class on this channel, or `None` when the store's table has no row —
a configuration error the till surfaces rather than papers over with zero.

MenuResponse.description:
The store's price book, as the in-store UI reads it.

The capability flags are flat and stay flat. `struct_excessive_bools` is a good lint about
*arguments* — four positional bools at a call site is a bug waiting to happen — and this struct
is never constructed positionally: it is serialized, and each flag is named on the wire by a
field a till reads by name. Grouping them under a `capabilities` object is the shape B5.3 will
want when the rest arrive, and it is **not available now**: `tips_enabled` and `seats_enabled`
are already published, and `AGENTS.md` §2 forbids removing or renaming a published field —
nesting them would do exactly that to every till that has not updated yet (ADR-0111's
one-directional version rule is what makes an old device safe, and only while this is additive).
When a sixth flag needs a reader, the answer is a *new* nested object beside these, with these
deprecated rather than moved.

accepted_tender.description:
The payment methods this store accepts, as their wire names, or `None` when the store
restricts nothing and every method is on ([ADR-0080](../../../docs/adr/0080-channels-and-tender.md)).

`None` rather than "all seven listed" so the till can tell "no restriction published" from "a
restriction that happens to allow everything" — and so a method added to the enum later is
accepted by an unrestricted store without a config change.

courses.description:
The courses any item above goes out on, **in service order**
([ADR-0130](../../../../docs/adr/0130-a-course-is-something-the-catalog-names.md)).

Joins this response in the change that consumes it, which is the rule this module's header
sets: the course picker that fires "starters away" is in this change, and the compiled book
has carried these only since the change before it.

Already sorted, ties broken by id, by the cloud compiler. A till must render them in the
order given and must not sort them again: the sequence is the entity's whole meaning, and a
screen that rebuilt it from a filtered list is how "main" ends up before "starter".

Empty on a store that has published none, which is every store until the console authors
one — and the till then offers no course control, exactly as it did before this field.

courses_enabled.description:
Whether this store groups its lines into courses (§10 `Capability::Courses`, on by default).

The flag that decides whether the till offers a course control at all. A counter that fires
everything at once has no starters to send, and `POST /api/orders/{id}/fire/{course_id}`
refuses a store with this off — so offering the control there would be an action the edge
will not honour, the same failure `tips_enabled` was added to stop.

currency.description: The store's currency — every amount below is in it.

items.description:
The items, in the order the store published them. Each rate is already resolved for the
channel a walk-in sale arrives on, so the till never picks a channel of its own.

kds_enabled.description:
Whether fired lines reach a kitchen display (§10 `Capability::Kds`, on by default).

Rides with `tables_enabled` because it answers the same question about the same screen: a
destination in the status bar that leads to a board this store does not run is an offer the
store cannot honour, which is the same failure `tips_enabled` was added to stop.

modifier_groups.description:
Every modifier group any item above attaches, listed once
([ADR-0127](../../../../docs/adr/0127-modifier-groups-reach-the-edge.md)).

Empty on a store that has published none, which is every store until the console attaches
one — and the till then asks nothing, exactly as it did before this field existed.

seats_enabled.description:
Whether this store assigns items to seats (§10 `Capability::Seats`, authored on the
`capabilities` node, and **off by default** — most counters have no seats to speak of).

Joins this response in the change that consumes it, which is the rule this module's header
sets: `seat` has ridden `sales.order_line.added` and `LineDraft` since they were written, the
add route has accepted it all along, and nothing has ever set it — because the till had no way
to know whether the store wanted to be asked.

split_ways_max.description:
The most guests the pay screen's even split offers, from the store's `tender_keys` node
(ADR-0160 decision 2): it offers every number from two up to this one. `6` until a store sets
its own, at most `12`. A till reading an edge older than the field offers two to six.

tables_enabled.description:
Whether this store runs table service (§10 `Capability::Tables`, **on** by default).

The one flag that decides what the till's home screen is. A counter cafe has no floor plan,
and `Capability::PayFirst` is declared incompatible with this one in the capability model's
own validity rules — so a store with it off being shown a room full of tables it does not
have is not a cosmetic problem, it is the till describing a different shop.

tip_percents.description:
The tip keys the pay screen offers, each a whole percentage of the bill, in the order the
store's `tender_keys` node names them: a key set to `0`, or to a percentage an earlier key
offers, is left out
([ADR-0160](../../../../docs/adr/0160-everything-a-store-runs-differently-is-published-configuration.md)
decision 2). `[5, 10, 15]` until a store sets its own, and empty when no key is left, which
the till takes as no tip row at all.

Beside `tips_enabled`, which still decides whether the till asks for a tip at all. A till
older than the field ignores it, and a till reading an edge older than the field offers the
three keys it always did.

tips_enabled.description:
Whether this store takes tips (§10 `Capability::Tips`, authored on the `capabilities` node).

The till shows no tip entry when this is false, which is the difference between a guest being
offered something the edge will refuse and the action simply not being there.

walk_in_channel.description:
The channel the counter opens a walk-in on, from the store's `counter` node (ADR-0160
decision 2): `WALK_IN_CHANNEL_TAKEAWAY` until a store sets its own, `WALK_IN_CHANNEL_DINE_IN`,
or `WALK_IN_CHANNEL_ASK`, where the cashier asks each guest. A value the edge cannot read is
sent as takeaway, the channel it opens such a store's walk-ins on.

The counter shows a walk-in the book of the channel it opens on. A till older than the field
ignores it, and a till reading an edge older than the field shows the takeaway book, the
channel that edge opens every walk-in on.

MergeRequest.description: The bills a merge folds into the target.

MergeResponse.description: The surviving bill and everything it now covers.

MintedCode.description: The minted code, and when it stops working.

code.description:
The six digits the next device presents. **This response body is the only place it exists** —
it is not written to a file and not logged, so a caller that loses this reply mints another.

expires_at_ms.description:
When the code expires, Unix ms. Returned rather than a duration so a till can show a
countdown without assuming this box's `CODE_TTL`, which is a constant a fork may change.

ModifierGroupId.description: A `ModifierGroupId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

ModifierGroupResponse.description: One modifier group, as the till asks it.

display_name.description:
The name to show, already in the store's display language — the same resolution the item's
own name gets ([ADR-0074](../../../../docs/adr/0074-localization-and-tax.md)).

max_select.description: How many choices a guest may make at most.

member_menu_item_ids.description:
The items offered as choices. Each is an ordinary item in `items` above, with its own price
— which is how a large pizza costs more than a small one without a second pricing concept.

min_select.description:
How many choices a guest must make. **Zero means optional**; the till has no separate
`required` flag to disagree with this number, and neither does the book.

modifier_group_id.description: The group's identifier, which an item above names.

Money.description:
An amount of money: an integer count of the currency's minor unit.

The wire form is `{"currency_code": "VND", "amount_minor": 150000}`, and the
database form is `char(3)` plus `bigint`. Both halves travel together always —
an amount without its currency is not money, it is a number.

amount_minor.description: Whole minor units: đồng for VND, yen for JPY, cents for USD.

MovementRequest.description:
A paid in or a paid out: how much, in minor units, and why (ADR-0165 decision 1), and the
approver for a drawer assigned to somebody else.

NumberFormat.description:
How a country writes numbers.

Held as separators rather than as a format string, because a format string is a small language
and every small language eventually needs an escape rule. Grouping is *digits per group* so that
India's 2-2-3 lakh grouping is expressible later by widening this field rather than by replacing
the type.

decimal_separator.description: Between the integer and fractional parts. `.` in Vietnam and Japan, `,` in much of Europe.

digits_per_group.description: Digits per group, counting from the decimal separator.

group_separator.description: Between groups of digits. `.` in Vietnam, `,` in Japan.

OpenDrawerRequest.description: Opening the drawer outside a sale: why, and the manager whose PIN allows it (ADR-0165 decision 3).

OpenDrawerResponse.description: What a no-sale opening reports: the opening is recorded, and this is whether the drawer sprang.

OpenOrderRequest.description:
A walk-in order as the counter asks for it (ADR-0146). Without a channel it takes the store's
walk-in channel, `counter.walk_in_channel`: takeaway, the ordinary counter order, unless the store
sets its walk-ins to be eaten in (ADR-0160 decision 2).

OpenPaymentMethod_PaymentMethod.description: A `PaymentMethod` token: PAYMENT_METHOD_UNSPECIFIED, PAYMENT_METHOD_CASH, PAYMENT_METHOD_CARD, PAYMENT_METHOD_QR, PAYMENT_METHOD_VOUCHER, PAYMENT_METHOD_GIFT_CARD, PAYMENT_METHOD_OTHER, or one a newer build sent, which is kept as it arrived

OpenReceiptLanguage_ReceiptLanguage.description: A `ReceiptLanguage` token: RECEIPT_LANGUAGE_UNSPECIFIED, RECEIPT_LANGUAGE_DISPLAY, RECEIPT_LANGUAGE_COUNTRY, RECEIPT_LANGUAGE_VI, RECEIPT_LANGUAGE_EN, or one a newer build sent, which is kept as it arrived

OpenRequest.description:
Opening a shift with a starting float, on the device's own till's drawer or the one it names.
Another till's also takes an approver where the person holds that only with approval
(ADR-0167 decision 3).

oneOf.description:
The person another till's drawer is for, where the store assigns drawers: somebody on its
roster. A drawer started at its own till is the starter's, and this is ignored there.

assigned_staff_code.description:
The same person by their staff code, which is what a till types. Read only where
`assigned_employee_id` is absent; a code nobody on the roster has names nobody.

oneOf.description:
Another till's drawer to open, where the store keeps one per till. Absent is the device's
own, and where the store keeps one drawer it is ignored.

OpenSalesChannel_SalesChannel.description: A `SalesChannel` token: SALES_CHANNEL_UNSPECIFIED, SALES_CHANNEL_DINE_IN, SALES_CHANNEL_TAKEAWAY, SALES_CHANNEL_DELIVERY, SALES_CHANNEL_QR, SALES_CHANNEL_API, or one a newer build sent, which is kept as it arrived

OpenedOrderResponse.description: A walk-in order the counter has just opened, with the number the guest will be called by.

OrderId.description: A `OrderId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

OrderLineId.description: A `OrderLineId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

OrderLineRequest.description:
A line as the counter adds it to an order by id: what the guest chose, and no price — the
edge prices it at the order's own channel (ADR-0146).

note.description: The guest's note for the kitchen, held in memory and never logged (ADR-0157).

note_present.description: Deprecated by `note`: a device that sends only the flag still records that a note exists.

PairAccepted.description: The token issued to a successfully paired device.

device_token.description: The opaque bearer token the device presents on later requests.

PairRequest.description: A device presenting a pairing code.

code.description: The six-digit code the operator read from the edge.

PairedDeviceView.description: One paired device as the console sees it.

device_id.description: The device id — what `POST /api/pair/revoke` takes back.

this_device.description:
Whether this is the device making the request. The one fact that lets an operator tell their
own tablet from the others, and the row they must **not** retire by accident: doing so signs
this browser out mid-service.

PairingState.description: The state of this store's device pairing, for the operator console.

devices.description: How many devices the store has admitted.

durable.description:
Whether those survive a restart (ADR-0091). Reported because an operator planning a reboot
mid-service needs to know whether it will cost them the fleet.

paired.description: Each paired device, newest first — what the operator picks from to retire a lost till.

PaymentRequest.description:
One payment a device applies to a bill: how it was paid, what the guest handed over, what was put
against the total, and what they left. Change is what is left of `tendered` once
`applied_to_bill` and `tip` are taken out of it.

`method` arrives as an [`Open`] enum so an unrecognised token is a clean rejection rather than a
deserialise failure; [`Self::into_payment`] is the domain boundary that refuses an unspecified or
unknown method.

oneOf.description:
The tip on this tender. Optional, so a device that takes no tips — or one built before the
field existed — settles exactly as before. It replaces the request's `tips` list, which
carried tips beside the payments with no correspondence to them (roadmap **B1.3**).

A line of text.

The framework decides between this and [`Self::Bitmap`] using
[`PrinterCapabilities::needs_bitmap`]; an adapter receiving `Text` sends it as text.

Text.description:
A line of text.

The framework decides between this and [`Self::Bitmap`] using
[`PrinterCapabilities::needs_bitmap`]; an adapter receiving `Text` sends it as text.

oneOf.description:
A pre-rendered raster image: one bit per pixel, rows padded to whole bytes.

Carries the width so an adapter need not infer it, because inferring it from the
byte count requires knowing the height, and getting that wrong shears the image.

Bitmap.description:
A pre-rendered raster image: one bit per pixel, rows padded to whole bytes.

Carries the width so an adapter need not infer it, because inferring it from the
byte count requires knowing the height, and getting that wrong shears the image.

oneOf.description: A QR code — a table link for guest ordering, or an invoice lookup code.

QrCode.description: A QR code — a table link for guest ordering, or an invoice lookup code.

oneOf.description: Cut the paper. Ignored by a printer that cannot.

Open the cash drawer wired to this printer: the kick
([ADR-0167](../../../docs/adr/0167-a-till-has-its-own-cash-drawer.md) decision 6).

A kick travels to a print agent as a job of its own, this block alone
([`PrintDocument::kick`]), and the agent opens the drawer through
[`PrinterDriver::open_drawer`], under its USB-only rule. It is never encoded into a
document's bytes, so anywhere else it opens nothing. An agent built before it cannot read it,
which is why the edge sends one only to an agent that says it carries a kick.

PrintBlock.description: One element of a printed document.

PrintJob.description:
A print job.

`job_id` is the idempotency key. Reprinting is a deliberate act with its own permission
and its own audit trail (`docs/pos-spec.md` §12 counts reprint rates per employee), so a
retry after an ambiguous failure must not silently produce a second ticket.

job_id.description: Idempotency key. A retry reuses it; a reprint mints a new one.

oneOf.description:
Which station's printer, or `None` for a job that no station made — the guest's receipt,
which comes off the counter's printer when the bill settles
([ADR-0100](../../../docs/adr/0100-receipt-and-ticket-printing.md)).

Optional rather than a nil id: a receipt genuinely has no station, and a placeholder would
have to be recognised as "not really a station" by everything that reads this.

PrintResponse.description:
What printing pre-bills came to: one outcome per document, in the order they were sent.

A list because a split table prints one pre-bill per open part, and a printer can take the first
and jam on the second; the till says which.

code_page.description: The character set its firmware renders directly.

columns.description:
Characters per line in the standard font. Receipt layout is computed from this, so
a wrong value produces wrapped totals.

dots_per_line.description:
Printable dots per line — the width of a raster this printer will accept.

Separate from [`columns`](Self::columns) because the two answer different questions and
neither derives from the other: `columns` is how much *text* fits, which depends on the
firmware's font, while this is how wide a *bitmap* may be, which is a property of the print
head. The common values are 384 for 58 mm paper and 576 for 80 mm, both at 203 dpi.

A raster wider than this is not clipped by the printer — the excess wraps onto the next
line and shears the image — so [ADR-0102](../../../docs/adr/0102-printing-any-script.md)
makes the renderer take this as its width rather than guess.

kicks_drawer.description: Whether a cash drawer is wired to it.

prints_bitmaps.description: Whether it can print raster images, which is what bitmap fallback needs.

PrinterResponse.description: One published printer, as the Devices screen lists it.

station_id.description: The station it serves, absent for the receipt printer.

Quantity.description:
A quantity, counted in thousandths of a unit.

The wire form is the integer count of thousandths, so 1.5 is `1500`. Naming it
`milli` rather than `value` keeps the scale visible at every use site.

QuantityRequest.description:
How many a line should now be.

A quantity and nothing else. Unlike an add, no money crosses this boundary: the edge holds the
unit price the device captured when the line was added, so it extends the line itself rather than
being told what the line comes to. One less number a caller can get wrong, and one less way for a
guest to be charged a total that does not follow from the price they were quoted.

Ratio.description:
An exact rational rate: a tax rate, a service charge, a percentage discount.

A rate is never a float. 10% is `Ratio::percent(10)`, which is 10/100 exactly,
and 8.25% is `Ratio::basis_points(825)`.

On the wire it is two integers, `{"numerator": 10, "denominator": 100}`. It has to
cross a boundary because a line snapshot captures **the tax rate in force at the
moment the line was added** (`docs/pos-spec.md` §14.2) — sending a decimal string
or a float instead would reintroduce exactly the imprecision the integer discipline
exists to prevent. `NonZeroI64` means a zero denominator is unrepresentable, so a
malformed rate is rejected at the edge rather than dividing by zero later.

ReasonCodeId.description: A `ReasonCodeId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

ReasonCodeResponse.description:
One entry a picker may offer: the id an event carries, the code a report groups by, the name in
the store's display language, and the actions it may be cited for.

applies_to.description: The `REASON_ACTION_*` tokens this entry declares, so one read serves every picker.

ReasonCodesResponse.description: The store's managed list, as the in-store UI reads it.

RejectReasonResponse.description: One reason the till may offer for a refusal — id to send back, name to show.

ReprintResponse.description: What a copy's press reports back to the till (ADR-0164).

copy_number.description: Which copy this was, counting from 1.

receipt_print.description: What came of the printing, as the settle reports it: `PRINTED`, `NO_PRINTER`, and so on.

RevokeRequest.description: Which device to retire. An absent `device_id` means every device.

device_id.description: The device to retire, or `None` for all of them.

RoutingRule.description:
One item→station routing rule: a fired line matching it routes to `station_id`.

A rule matches by a specific item or by a course; an item match takes precedence over a course
match (`pos_core::floor::route_station`). A rule that names neither is meaningless — the validator
rejects it rather than let it sit as a silent no-op.

course_id.description: Match any line on a course.

menu_item_id.description: Match a specific item. Takes precedence over a course match.

station_id.description: The station a matching line routes to.

SeatRequest.description:
How many guests were seated, if whoever seated them said.

Reporting data (average check per cover), never a gate: a seat with no body at all is the
request every device sent before B1.2 and still means "seat the table, count unknown".

SessionState.description: The current sign-in on a device, for the UI to restore its state after a reload.

idle_lock_seconds.description:
How many seconds an attended till may sit untouched before it signs its person out and
locks, from the store's `session` node
([ADR-0160](../../../../docs/adr/0160-everything-a-store-runs-differently-is-published-configuration.md));
`0` never locks. A fact about the store rather than the person, so it is sent whoever is
signed in. The till keeps the time, because what counts as a touch is what happens on its
screen.

lease_standing.description:
Whether a replacement machine has taken this store — `active`, `superseded` or `invalid`
([ADR-0123](../../../../docs/adr/0123-a-superseded-box-opens-nothing-new.md)).

On this route rather than a new one because it is the call the app already makes before it
draws anything, and because the state is a fact about the *box*, not about who is signed in:
a superseded till should say so on its sign-in screen, before anybody tries to seat a table.

opening_float_minor.description:
The float the Shift screen fills in when a shift opens, in the store currency's minor unit,
from the store's `shift` node (ADR-0160 decision 2); `0` fills in nothing. A store fact like
the idle lock, sent whoever is signed in. The cashier may change it, and the shift opens with
what they send.

permissions.description:
The permission ids the signed-in person holds directly, sorted. Empty when nobody is signed
in. The till hides what is in neither list once the store enforces them; the edge stays the
authority and refuses it anyway.

permissions_enforced.description:
Whether the store decides with each person's own set
([ADR-0158](../../../../docs/adr/0158-the-till-enforces-each-persons-own-permissions.md)
decision 6). `false`: every control works as before, and the two lists below are what the
person's roles say, not what the store enforces.

permissions_with_approval.description:
The permission ids the signed-in person holds only with approval, sorted: the till asks for
an approver before sending the act.

sign_in_ready.description:
Whether anyone can sign in on this box: at least one published member of staff has a PIN
([`StaffRoster::sign_in_ready`](crate::app::StaffRoster::sign_in_ready)).

It says nothing about any one badge code. It lets the sign-in screen tell a store the
console has not staffed yet from a mistyped PIN; the refusal alone answers both the same.

SettleRequest.description:
A settle request: the payments applied, each carrying the tip taken on it (a separate ledger,
never part of the total), and — for a B2B sale — who the tax invoice is for.

No `Debug`: it can carry a buyer, and a derived one would put that person's name into any log
line or rejection message that touched the request (`AGENTS.md` §2).

approver_code.description:
The approver for cash into a drawer assigned to somebody else (ADR-0167 decision 9): a code
and PIN, both or neither.

oneOf.description:
The corporate customer the invoice is issued to
([ADR-0107](../../../../docs/adr/0107-the-buyer-is-a-subject.md)). Absent on every ordinary
retail sale, and `#[serde(default)]` so a till built before this field existed settles
exactly as it did.

SettledBillResponse.description:
One of today's settled bills, as the till lists it to print a copy from
([ADR-0164](../../../../docs/adr/0164-a-receipt-is-reprinted-as-a-marked-copy-and-every-reprint-is-counted.md)).

copies.description: How many copies have been printed.

settle_clock.description:
The shop's wall clock when it settled, `HH:MM` in the store's timezone, for the list to show
as it is: a till's own clock may keep another zone, and the list is today's, so the date
would say nothing. Absent in the one case the calendar cannot read the instant.

table_id.description:
The table it was paid at, which the till shows by the floor's label. Absent for a counter
order, which shows its queue number instead.

ShiftId.description: A `ShiftId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

ShiftResponse.description: A shift as returned to a device after a command.

assigned_employee_id.description:
The person the drawer is assigned to for this session, where the store assigns drawers:
an id, never a name. Absent where drawers are shared.

day_ended.description:
`true` while the shift is still open past the business day it opened on, which a till and
the console flag (ADR-0167 decision 11). Absent otherwise.

drawer_open.description:
What came of opening the drawer, on a paid in or a paid out: `OPENED`, `NO_DRAWER` or
`DRAWER_UNAVAILABLE`. Absent on every other command.

expected_amount.description: Revealed at close (§11.1), and before it only where the store's count is not blind.

paid_in_amount.description: Cash paid into the drawer outside a sale so far (ADR-0165).

paid_out_amount.description: Cash paid out of it outside a sale so far.

shift_report_print.description:
What came of printing the shift report, on the close that asked for one — the same wire
tokens a settle reports its receipt with. Absent on every other command.

terminal_device_id.description: The till whose drawer it is, absent for the store's one drawer (ADR-0167).

variance.description: Revealed only at close. Negative means short.

SignInRequest.description: A sign-in: the badge `code` a person types and their `pin`. Both are secrets and never logged.

SignedIn.description: A successful sign-in: the employee the device now acts as.

SoldOutResponse.description: What marking an item sold out, or restoring it, answers: the item, and whether it is now sold out.

SplitRequest.description: The parts a split proposes, each the order lines one new bill will cover.

SplitResponse.description: The bills a split produced, in the order the parts were given.

StandingResponse.description: This box's activation standing, for the boot gate and the UI.

activated.description: `true` once a device credential is in the vault.

state_access.description:
Whether the store's state is closed to other local accounts (ADR-0174 decision 5). Absent
from a router that was given no state directory, and from an edge older than the field.

StateAccess.description: Whether the store's state is closed to other local accounts.

StationId.description: A `StationId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

StationPlan.description:
The store's kitchen plan: its stations, the routing rules that place a fired line on one, and the
default station a line with no matching rule falls to.

An empty plan is a store whose kitchen has not been published — the edge keeps whatever it holds.

default_station_id.description:
The station a fired line falls to when no routing rule matches. `None` means the store has no
catch-all — a line with no matching rule routes nowhere and the caller keeps its own fallback.

StoreId.description: A `StoreId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

SubcategoryResponse.description: One display sub-category: a second grouping level with its own buttons.

SyncResponse.description: The cloud link and the outbox, as a device draws them.

clock_drift.description:
`CLOCK_DRIFT_OK`, `CLOCK_DRIFT_ALARM` past `clock_drift_alarm_ms`, or
`CLOCK_DRIFT_UNSPECIFIED` when no probe has succeeded since the edge started.

clock_drift_alarm_ms.description: The offset either way past which the clock alarms, in milliseconds.

clock_measure_time.description: When that was measured, on this box's own clock; absent until measured.

clock_offset_ms.description: This box's clock minus the time server's, in milliseconds; absent until measured.

last_sync_time.description: When the outbox drain last reached the cloud; absent if it has not since the edge started.

outbox_depth.description: Events committed on this box and not yet acknowledged by the cloud.

outbox_planned_depth.description: The depth the warnings are graded against. Not a limit: the store sells past it.

TableId.description: A `TableId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

TableResponse.description: A table as returned to a device.

table_id.description: The table id, as a ULID string.

TakingsResponse.description: What the store has taken today, as the Today screen's tile shows it.

bill_count.description: How many bills settled that day.

business_date.description: The business day the figure is for.

takings_amount.description: What the day's settled bills came to: what their guests paid.

TaxClassId.description: A `TaxClassId`: a ULID, 26 Crockford base-32 characters

TaxComponentName.description:
A tax component's name as a bill records it: two to eight upper-case ASCII letters and digits,
starting with a letter, such as `CGST`, `SGST`, `UTGST`, `IGST` or `CESS`
([ADR-0168](../../../docs/adr/0168-a-settled-bill-records-its-tax-components.md) decision 1).

Built only through [`Self::new`], and refused on deserialise when it fails the check. A settled
bill's line reads such a name as *not split* rather than refusing the bill
([`crate::events::BillTaxLine::components`]). A country that prints other words maps the token
to them in its pack.

The personal-data barrier admits it to an event payload ([`crate::pii`]): it names a tax, and
eight characters with no space, `@` or lower case cannot carry a person's name, an e-mail or a
phone number. It comes from the `tax` node an operator authors, never from a till's input.

TerminalResponse.description: One published terminal, and whether a device holds it.

agent_device_id.description: The `TERMINAL` entry's id, which a claim and a release name.

name.description: The name the console gave the terminal.

TerminalsResponse.description: The store's terminals, as the till's **This device** card lists them.

terminals.description: The published `TERMINAL` entries, in the order the `devices` node lists them.

unlisted_agent_device_id.description:
The terminal **this** device holds when the `devices` node does not list it, which a release
names. Absent when this device holds a listed terminal or none.

A claim does not look the terminal up in the node, so a device can be bound by hand to an id
the node does not list. Without this the card says the device is none of the store's tills, a
bind answers that it is already another, and nothing on a screen can release it. Only ever
the caller's own binding: never another device's, and never a person.

TestPrintResponse.description:
What came of a test page: the same token a receipt's print reports (`PRINTED`, `NO_PRINTER`,
`PRINTER_UNAVAILABLE`, …).

TextStyle.description: Text styling. Deliberately minimal — a receipt is a document, not a design.

double_size.description: Double height and width, for a total or a queue number.

ThisDevice.description: The calling device, as [`this_device`] answers for it.

accepted.description:
Always `true`. A token the edge does not accept never gets this far: it is refused `401`.
Carried so the answer says what it means, and so a caller can tell it apart from the
`index.html` an edge older than this route answers for any path it does not know.

pair_time.description: When the calling device paired, RFC 3339 UTC.

Timestamp.description: An instant in UTC, as RFC 3339

TransferRequest.description: Where the guests are moving to.

to_table_id.description: The free table they move to, as a ULID string.

TransferResponse.description: What a move did, as returned to a device: the order that moved, and both tables after it.

from_table.description: The table the guests left, now waiting to be cleared.

order_id.description: The order that moved, as a ULID string.

to_table.description: The table they moved to, now seated with their order.

VarianceReason.description: The reason for one drawer's over or short, in a batch close.

VoidBillRequest.description:
A bill void as a till asks for it: the reason from the store's managed list, plus the manager's
badge and PIN — which, unlike a line's, are needed every time.

VoidBillResponse.description: The state a voided bill came to rest in, so the till can show it rather than re-reading.

VoidLineRequest.description:
A void as a till asks for it: the reason from the store's managed list, plus the manager's badge
and PIN when the line has already fired.

The approval is optional in the shape and required by the act — a line that never fired needs
none, and one that has cannot proceed without it. Making it optional here rather than splitting
the route in two keeps the till's one control talking to one endpoint: the till does not have to
know the fired/unfired rule, and the edge, which does, answers `403` when the PIN is the missing
piece.

approver_code.description: The approving manager's badge code, when one is needed.

approver_pin.description: The approving manager's PIN. Never logged and never stored.

WaitingLineResponse.description: One line of a waiting order, so staff can see what the guest asked for before agreeing to it.

WaitingOrderResponse.description: One guest order waiting for a member of staff.

table_id.description:
The table the guest scanned. Always present: a held order is a tabled QR order by
definition (ADR-0116), and a screen that could not say which table would be useless.

WaitingResponse.description:
The queue, plus the reasons a refusal may cite.

One response rather than two reads: the picker is only ever opened from this screen, and a
till that had to fetch the reasons separately could show a refusal dialog with nothing in it.

WaiveFeeRequest.description:
A fee waive as a till asks for it: the reason from the store's managed list, plus the badge
and PIN of somebody who holds `billing.fee.waive` where the person acting needs one
([ADR-0159](../../../../docs/adr/0159-a-fee-is-configuration.md) decision 5).

till_session.description: The token a device is issued when it is paired, presented as a bearer token. On `/ws` a browser offers it as the second WebSocket subprotocol instead, because an upgrade cannot carry an Authorization header.
